source.title: Decomposing a factorial into large factors

best_human.provenance: Reconstruction of the repository's greedy large-factor method attributed in its source comment to Andrew Sutherland's Maple program, with Adam Wagner credited for assistance in translating it to Python. This implementation constructs a threshold-33330 divisor with at least N factors, then restores all remaining prime powers across exactly N retained factors.
best_human.ai_provenance: The source does not state whether AI tools were used. No AI-free claim is made.
best_human.evidence_state: full 100000-factor witness independently rechecked by exact product and Legendre-prime-exponent tests

best_public.evidence_state: archived LP lower-bound endpoint; the text file contains no per-instance factorization witness and this endpoint was not independently reproduced
best_public.ai_provenance: Not stated by the source; the repository describes linear/integer programming and greedy construction.

best_reproduced.reproduction_status: exactly rechecked; all factors positive; exactly 100000 factors; product exactly 100000!

frozen_human_baseline.evidence_state: reconstructed from pinned upstream greedy algorithm and independently verified

public_reported_interval.endpoint_semantics: bounding_data.py returns (Tlb,Tub): the lower endpoint advances only when the greedy procedure finds at least N admissible factors; the upper endpoint comes from the LP relaxation and its dual bound.
public_reported_interval.limitations: The public archive has no 100000-specific factor witness. The paper states that upper bounds in the relevant numerical figures were not verified. The generator also notes its factor-at-most-N modeling assumption had not yet been rigorously proved. Do not treat 33649 as an unconditional certified upper bound.

rigorous_published_bound.upper_bound_source: Theorem 1.3(i), arXiv:2503.20170v4: t(N) <= N/e for N not in {1,2,4}; for N=100000 this implies integer t(N) <= floor(100000/e)=36787.
rigorous_published_bound.status: exact optimum remains open in the sources checked

T053-C01.survey_scope_note: The repository main branch still points to commit 978e4802dd413356e7e0ff97a44db803ab9596eb on 2026-11-06. The 2026 journal publication and arXiv v4 do not report an exact t(100000) value. The public LP interval is kept separate from the rigorous published upper bound.
